labels.note: Equal-priority shared rule is pushed from anotherArray, then again from array: duplicate rule in merged output.
Equal priorities take the > branch, so the same rule is pushed twice; the dedupe branch is never reached.
Equal priorities no longer advance the indices, so the loop never ends when both arrays share a rule.
A rule present in both arrays is skipped, silently losing a permission rule from the merged result.
With equal priorities i goes backwards: array[-1] throws at index 0, otherwise earlier rules are reprocessed or duplicated.
With equal priorities j goes backwards: throws at index 0 or repeats earlier anotherArray rules.
Leftover rules of the first array are dropped whenever anotherArray runs out first; common path loses permission rules.
